text.content:
Make it yours

This module is a template. Before you put anything in it, give it its own identity, or it will clash with anyone else using the starter kit:

  1. Close Foundry (or return to Setup).
  2. Copy the folder Data/modules/essence20-homebrew-starter and rename the copy - for example my-ranger-homebrew. Lower case, numbers and hyphens only.
  3. Open the copy's module.json and change id to exactly the new folder name. Change title, description and authors.
  4. Optionally rename the compendium labels (label in packs) and the folder name in packFolders.
  5. Start Foundry, turn your module on in the world, and open its compendiums.

A compendium from a module is locked. Right-click it in the Compendium tab and choose Toggle Edit Lock to add and change items. Your changes are saved into your module's folder, ready to share.

One compendium per kind of thing

CompendiumItem types
PerksPerk
Powers and SpellsPower, Spell, Magic Bauble
Roles and OriginsRole, Role Points, Focus, Origin, Influence, Hang-Up, Bond, Faction
Gear and WeaponsWeapon, Weapon Effect, Armor, Shield, Gear, Upgrade, Equipment Package, Alteration
Zord and Transformer FeaturesFeature, Megaform Trait, Alt Mode, Trait
Threats and NPCsActors: NPCs, Zords, Vehicles, Companions

Nothing forces this split - any item can go in any Item compendium - but it keeps the Compendium Browser and your players' searches tidy. Delete the compendiums you don't need from module.json.

pages.name: Showing up in the Compendium Browser

text.content:
The Compendium Browser finds your items by itself

Every Item compendium Foundry has loaded is in the browser - nothing to register. How each part of it is filled:

In the browserComes from
The book groupsThe compendium's folder (packFolders in module.json). This kit uses "Homebrew". To list your books with a game line instead, name the folder exactly like that line's: GI Joe, My Little Pony, Power Rangers, Transformers or Welcome to Night Vale.
The book name on each rowThe compendium's label
The pageThe item's Source page (its Details)
The tabsThe item type
The sub-filter on a tabA Perk's or Power's type, a Focus's items
Traits, Gear Type, AvailabilityA weapon's, armor's or shield's traits; gear's Gear Type; a Power's Availability
"Qualifies for"The item's prerequisites
SearchThe item's name

A GM can switch any compendium off under Configure Sourcebooks; the world's Game Line setting never switches off a module's compendiums.

pages.name: Making it work: the Rules tab

text.content:
Automate with rules, not descriptions

An item does things through the rules on its Rules tab - a Perk that gives Edge, a Power that raises a Defense, an item that reacts when its owner is hit. The description is only for people to read; the system never reads it.

  • Open the item, go to Rules, and add a rule. Each rule type explains its fields, and the editor tells you when a rule would change nothing.
  • The example Perk, Example: Steady Under Fire, has one rule: a Roll Modifier that gives Edge on Targeting Tests.
  • Copying a working item from the system's own compendiums is the fastest way to learn a rule type: drag it into your compendium, then change it.
  • Fill in Automation on the item - full, partial or manual, with a note - so players know what happens by itself and what the GM handles.

Who can take it

An item's Prerequisites say who qualifies: a Skill at a die size, an Essence score, a Role or Perk already taken, and so on. They drive the green tick or red cross on the sheet and the browser's "Qualifies for" filter, and - depending on the world's setting - a warning or a block when someone takes it.

The example Perk needs Targeting at d4 or better. Anything the system can't check (a GM's say-so) can go in the prerequisite notes instead.

Your words, not the book's

  • Don't paste rulebook text into descriptions. Describe what your item does in your own words, and put the book and page in its Source if it's based on one.
  • Don't include official art, logos or stat blocks from the Hasbro lines. They belong to Hasbro and are licensed to Renegade, not to us - fine for a private game, not for something you share.
  • Your own creations, your own descriptions and your own art (or art you have the rights to) are yours to share.

Giving it to other tables

  • Simplest: zip your module's folder and send it. They unzip it into Data/modules.
  • With updates: put it on GitHub, attach module.json and a zip of the folder to a release, and set manifest and download in module.json to those files' URLs. Others install it from the manifest URL in Foundry and get your updates.
  • Bump version in module.json every time you share a change.
